France Coach Didier Deschamps Steps Down After 14 Years

Didier Deschamps, the longest-serving manager of France's national team, has announced his retirement after 14 years in charge. The decision comes amid reports of a 'stifling atmosphere' within the team, with some outlets suggesting that this may have contributed to his departure. Deschamps led Les Bleus to major international success during his tenure, but the team's World Cup campaign ended in disappointment. His successor, Zinedine Zidane, is expected to take charge of the team.
